crime: A prisoner who could not sleep behind the cell bars spent her evenings asleep under the courtyard tree, wrapped in a blanket. {WITCH_NAME} sat beside her, brushing fallen leaves from her face. Her Magic let her hear the sleeping girl's heart quicken before she stirred, and each time she caught the girl's sleeve. At dusk she would come into the lounge and say, "She's asleep. Her heart's slow as ever." Every night at lockup, the others found the girl just so.
One dusk, the girl pulled her sleeve free of {WITCH_NAME}'s fingers. "You grab me every time I wake up. From tomorrow, I'm sleeping out here alone."

As a child, {WITCH_NAME} had fallen asleep with her ear on her mother's heart, but only on the nights her mother came home. Each time, she woke to an empty pillow. The warm ones leave while you sleep.
That dusk, as the girl drifted off, {WITCH_NAME} pressed a hand over her mouth and nose and held it there, listening, until the girl's heart stopped.

At eight that night, {WITCH_NAME}, who had sat in the lounge in full view of the others since dusk, cried out: "Another heart is pounding out there beside hers, and now hers has stopped!" The prisoners ran out and found the girl smothered under the tree. In the trial court, they ruled that she had been killed at eight by whoever owned that pounding heart, never by {WITCH_NAME}, who had sat among them.

But one prisoner had noticed the fallen leaves lying unbroken across the girl's lips and throat, a whole evening's fall. Then the prisoners understood. No hand had touched her at eight. She had died at dusk, when {WITCH_NAME} left her, and the heart she said she heard stop was a lie.
fields.epitaph: At last she kept the one who could never get up and leave, and had no heartbeat left to listen for.
execution: The execution stand raises an iron bed with an iron mother lying on it. The witch is chained on her side against it, her ear to its iron chest. Inside the chest, an iron heart begins to beat, each thud carrying through the whole court. At every beat, an iron arm draws her tighter against the chest. She stops stirring while the heart beats on. Then the iron mother rises from the bed and walks away across the court, her iron heart gone quiet. The witch lies still, her ear on the empty iron pillow.

magic.name: Ear to Every Heart
magic.text: She hears every heart around her, beat by beat, as clearly as a clock held to her ear.
